analysis:
Examined both workflow excerpts, changelog metadata/content, and the build-documentation patch. In .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml:794–806, 915–927, 1034–1046 and 1203–1215, the new selection step disables Actions caching for darkbloom-* runners lacking DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. Visible restore/save conditions consistently honor that flag, including audio fixtures (576, 587) and metadata builds (1126, 1164). The new .git checks (831–856, 952–977, 1064–1089, 1233–1258) reject links, non-sample hooks and specified executable/include configuration before integrity checks and checkout; checkout retains persist-credentials:false. These changes reduce existing cache exposure and do not establish a concrete security regression. Existing test gates, artifact reporting and build-cache timestamp reuse were also examined; no changed authorization, attestation, billing or inference-encryption behavior is visible.
The documentation and changelog describe CI caches, not the consumer KV cache governed by T-041; no change to that mitigation is evidenced. Artifact/source integrity is relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054, but these excerpts neither grant serving authorization nor qualify builds. Integration should verify the newly claimed repository-wide coverage against other changed workflows, provider-ci-build/provider-release-build composites and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (invoked at 1355). The runner-name and cache-URL/preload contract described in docs/developer/build.md:658–680 remains externally asserted, not verified here. Those dependencies affect the cache-isolation conclusion, so deeper integration review is needed; missing source is not evidence of a vulnerability.
